Key findings: (1) NL2-ENDPOINT-HWY/URBAN and NL2-DISJOINT-1 are satisfied by tr line 106/107 (InitialState->HighwayMode/UrbanMode) with distinct discrete triggers high_way_true/urban_way_true, so omitted. (2) NL7-DERIVED guard-disjointness and endpoint contracts for enter_urban are satisfied by distinct triggers (dist_to_front_15_extra_lane_true, road_clear, intersection_true), so omitted. (3) NL6/NL10 termination endpoint contracts are realized through composite-scoped completion edges (e.g., cruise->FinishState triggered dist_to_exit_2) and the top-level macro edges AutonomousMode->HighwayMode.FinishState (auto_finished_true), consistent with the documented macro/route-token compilation pattern in the working contract, so they remain satisfied and are omitted. (4) The single genuine structural gap is CollisionAvoidance composite reachability: exact_source_inventory and inspection_equivalent_facts show CollisionAvoidance (and its children collision_avoidance_deactive/collision_avoidance_active) have reachable_from_initial=false with STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL diagnostics at lines 89-91, and verify_facts confirms all three reachability checks refuted. decisions.reason: The NL requirement only states 'From the InitialState, the system can transition to either HighwayMode or UrbanMode' and does not specify an exact ownership scope for FinishState. The exact source facts show FinishState is first mentioned inside the HighwayMode block (line 15/its nested transitions), yet the closed ModelIR shows transitions from AutonomousMode (line 40) and UrbanMode (line 43) also target FinishState. Because the requirement text is silent on whether FinishState must be a top-level (root) final state shared across all top-level composite regions or a locally nested state reached indirectly through HighwayMode's boundary, two competent readings remain compatible with the same exact facts: (1) FinishState is a scope defect - it should be declared as a sibling/root-level state so all three composites (HighwayMode, AutonomousMode, UrbanMode) target the same shared instance directly, or (2) the closed model's routing, in which external transitions functionally reach 'the same FinishState' through the tool's declaration semantics (first-mention containment), is an accepted modeling convention that does not create a functional copy, since PlantUML/model tooling typically resolves same-named target states to one canonical element regardless of textual nesting. Because the predicate plan here has no usable frozen predicate (predicate_id=null, backend=unsupported/unknown), the underlying source and containment facts are exact and decisive that a genuine cross-scope structural tension exists, but the exact resolution (is this a benign single-state resolution by the modeling tool, or a genuine scope violation demanding a root-level FinishState) is not settled by the supplied dossier alone. This alternative reading is a competent undercutting defeater, not merely a possibility, because it is grounded in the exact containment/source facts supplied (first-mention line 15, and the three cross-scope target lines 40/41/43) rather than speculation.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The alternative reading is that the closed model's single named FinishState element is treated by the modeling tool/semantics as one canonical shared state regardless of which block's transition first mentions it, so the transitions from AutonomousMode (line 40) and UrbanMode (line 43) already reach the same FinishState element as the one declared via HighwayMode's line 15 mention, without creating any functional duplicate; under this reading the observed nesting is a harmless artifact of PlantUML's declare-by-first-mention convention rather than a structural containment defect.
decisions.violated_obligation: FinishState, an undeclared state whose first mention is inside the HighwayMode block (PlantUML line 15: 'cruise --> FinishState : dist_to_exit<2'), is also targeted by transitions originating outside HighwayMode (AutonomousMode --> FinishState at line 40, UrbanMode --> FinishState at line 43). The requirement's structure implies these external transitions should reach a single shared FinishState rather than being routed through HighwayMode's local child copy, so FinishState's containment under HighwayMode-only scope is in tension with its cross-scope use.

issues.basis: exact_source_inventory.transitions (complete 27-row inventory, none targeting CollisionAvoidance); inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL lines 89-91); verify_facts.non_proved (reachability checks for CollisionAvoidance, collision_avoidance_deactive, collision_avoidance_active all status=refuted); reference_inspection_facts W_UNREACHABLE_STATE diagnostics for collision_avoidance_deactive and collision_avoidance_active
issues.expected: CollisionAvoidance (and thus its collision_avoidance_deactive/collision_avoidance_active behavior) must be reachable from the model root/AutonomousMode so the described monitoring/activation behavior can execute.
issues.observed: exact_source_inventory lists CollisionAvoidance as a top-level composite (parent=null) with no incoming transition from AutonomousMode, InitialState, HighwayMode, or UrbanMode anywhere among the 27 authored transitions; inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts both confirm CollisionAvoidance, collision_avoidance_deactive, and collision_avoidance_active are unreachable from the top-level initial entry (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL, reachability checks refuted). The composite's own local initial edge (CollisionAvoidance -> collision_avoidance_deactive) is present and correctly targets its child, but this local entry can never fire because the composite itself is never entered.
issues.reason: NL12 requires the collision avoidance subsystem to begin in collision_avoidance_deactive and to respond to activation conditions; this behavior is only realized in the closed model. Structural contrast between the source's sibling-composite topology and the requirement that CollisionAvoidance's declared behavior actually execute reveals a composite-level reachability gap that is independent of the already-satisfied owner-local initial-entry edge.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue CollisionAvoidance is intentionally modeled as an always-active orthogonal region implicitly composed with AutonomousMode rather than a state reached via an explicit transition, in which case root-level entry semantics would not apply the same way; however, neither the source PlantUML nor the closed FCSTM declares CollisionAvoidance as a concurrent/orthogonal region of AutonomousMode (no region separator, no explicit concurrency declaration), so this rebuttal is not supported by the exact structural facts.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidance composite is structurally unreachable from root despite correct owner-local initial edge

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.states reachable_from_initial=false for state:collision_avoidance_deactive:line:90; verify_facts.checks reachability refuted for the same state; verify_facts.checks event-consumer refuted for the pedestrian-detection event whose sole consumer is this state's outgoing transition.
issues.expected: collision_avoidance_deactive must remain reachable and able to receive/consume the pedestrian/rear/front detection event so continuous monitoring can occur as described.
issues.observed: inspection_equivalent_facts marks state:collision_avoidance_deactive:line:90 with reachable_from_initial=false; verify_facts refutes reachability for this exact state and also refutes event-consumer reachability for the pedestrian/rear/front detection event (its only consumer transition:line:93 has reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]); the entire CollisionAvoidance composite is an isolated island with no incoming edge from AutonomousMode/HighwayMode/UrbanMode.
issues.reason: The NL establishes collision_avoidance_deactive as an operating monitoring state that must retain onward behavior (progress into collision_avoidance_active) whenever detection conditions hold. Root unreachability of the whole composite makes this retained behavior unobservable/unexecutable in the closed model, which is the deterministic deadlock/frontier evidence this contract's property targets.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The local outgoing transition (collision_avoidance_deactive -> collision_avoidance_active) exists and is well-formed in isolation, so if a future or alternate root wiring made CollisionAvoidance reachable, this exact local continuation would already be sufficient; the defect is entirely upstream (root reachability), not a locally malformed frontier.
issues.title: Collision avoidance monitoring subsystem is entirely unreachable, so its continuous-monitoring obligation cannot execute
